qt: to the Commission Barry Cowen (Renew) Subject:

Furthermore, can the Commission clarify the legal and policy basis for applying existing trade defence measures on biodiesel and hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) to US-origin SAF, including whether the potential impact on SAF availability, airline compliance with the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation, and Member States’ energy security objectives was assessed before this approach was adopted?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2026) The anti-dumping1 and anti-subsidy measures2 on biodiesel imports from the US, in force since 2009, apply to ‘fatty-acid mono-alkyl esters and/or paraffinic gasoils obtained from synthesis and/or hydro-treatment, of non-fossil origin’, including hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). These measures were imposed following thorough investigations which established that unfairly priced imports from the US caused injury to EU producers. The purpose of the measures is not to block imports but to restore fair competition and ensure a healthy biodiesel industry in the EU and continued investments in the sector. The Commission also adopted corrections via Implementing Regulations (EU) 2025/18613 and 2025/18694 to clarify the TARIC codes (TARif Intégré Communautaire; Integrated Tariff of the European Communities) for HEFA-SAF. These corrections were of a technical nature and did not change the nature and rationale of the existing acts. Therefore, no specific impact assessment was carried out as regards SAF availability, airline compliance with the ReFuelEU Aviation5 or the Member States’ energy security objectives. The Commission also recalls that no sustainable aviation fuels other than HEFA-SAF are currently subject to anti-dumping or countervailing duties. On 31 July 2026, the Commission initiated interim reviews6 of these measures with a view to investigate whether HEFA-SAF should be excluded. The industry will be consulted. Member States are part of the decision-making process.
